stem.text: Determine whether the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{2 n + 5}{2 n + 6} \), converges or diverges. Name a test whose conditions the series meets and state the verdict it gives.

answer_key.label: The series diverges by the nth term test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 1 \ne 0 \).

worked_solution.text: The general term \( \frac{2 n + 5}{2 n + 6} \) is a quotient of two linear expressions, so check its limit first with the nth term test.
worked_solution.rule_named: match the form to a test

worked_solution.text: Dividing the numerator and denominator by n gives \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{2 n + 5}{2 n + 6} = 1 \).
The series diverges by the nth term test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 1 \ne 0 \).

options.label: The series converges to \( 1 \), because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 1 \).
options.derivation: the limit of the sequence of terms reported as the sum of the series

options.label: The series diverges by the nth term test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = \frac{5}{6} \ne 0 \).
options.derivation: the limit of the terms evaluated by setting n to 0 instead of letting n grow

The series converges by the ratio test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right| = 1 \).
options.derivation: the ratio test named, but its requirement of a limit below 1 not checked when the ratio tends to 1
